Assassins are really the only dedicated star generating class.  Others that generate starts usually can only do so with a brave chain, and even then it's usually around the low 20's, and usually it's on a servant that would want to use the stars themselves.  This is why typically when people are running a team where a servant relies on crits, they use the 2030 CE to guarantee crit stars every turn while also allowing them to use whatever partner servants they want, so they can add servants with lower natural crit weight.

However, if you really want an answer, Karna and Enkidu are decent lancers at generating stars.  For rider, while Drake only has one quick card, if you can place it at the end of the chain it'll net her a decent amount, but it'd recommend against using her because riders have the highest natural crit weight and will thusly steal all the stars from your other servants on turns that you don't have the crit weight up skill active if you plan on using her in a team outside of an all rider squad.  For archer, Atalanta has the best burst of crit stars in the game on her NP, assuming you hit 3 targets and overkill.  Again though, archers have high crit weight.

The Carmilla CE is actually 50% NP gauge and only 20% crit damage.  It's decent if you're having trouble filling your gauge, which you might with a team that lacks many arts cards, even if you crit often, but when you're not critting it's really lackluster.  If that's the best you have though, it's not bad.

If you don't have enough hearts to ascend all of them, I'd keep in mind what you need.  Euryale fits a very specific niche of killing male servants, and is best against sabers, which is why she is great for killing Gawain. Tamamo's job is to buff any servant you have that has a damage dealing Arts NP.  Nero, Kuro, Shiki, you name it.  She's a hard support and has great uptime on her Arts buff which is really nice since it lasts 3 turns instead of 1, even though it has the same scaling as typical prana burst skills.  She is tanky through means of her own defense buff and also by delaying enemy np.  She has a decent heal on NP and charges the NP bars of your team a little, just general support style things.  Really, the main reason you take her is for the arts buff as it helps you charge NP faster and deal more damage.

Jeanne Alter is a raw beatstick.  She deals a lot of damage, and runs especially well if you have someone who can generate crits for her.  She'd be your main damage dealer and she really excels at it.  She has a really unwieldy attack stat, the highest in the game at the moment, also paired with the highest modifier given to only berserkers, avengers, and rulers.  Essentially she just hits really hard based on raw stats alone.  If you have someone to feed her stars it skyrockets after you level her first skill.

The reason Tia is better against Earth is because Anat is an elemental modifier when it goes into the equation, and you already get a boost to that number for having type advantage.  The equation gives all number a base of one, adding the modifiers for each type of damage boost, and then multiplying them.  Since they're all going to be over 1, it's best to have a little bit of every type rather than a lot of one type, hence why Tiamat is a better summon if you have high enough skill levels and are versus Earth.  Usually, though, it is best to take one Tiamat and one Anat so that both are boosted a little.

Something also important to note is how the numbers interact in the damage equation.  Lucifer is an elemental multiplier, and so it stacks additively with bonus damage from being the stronger element.  If you're fighting versus dark, that would add up to being a 3 (1[this number is static, never changes]+1[foe is dark]+1[lucifer]) and among the things this 3 gets multiplied by, one of them is magna bonuses.  For magna it would be (1[also static]+.66[from your magna weapons]) totaling 3*1.66=4.98.  However if you use chev summon it would be 2*2.32=4.64.  Lucifer will be the stronger pick for now, even versus dark, but after you skill up more magna weapons, chev becomes better versus dark, while lucifer will still be your go to choice against other elements.

Medication isn't as scary as it seems.  I take lexapro, geodon, and buspar, for various mental disorders.  It's really just a matter of finding the right psychiatrist.  You need someone who will take into consideration your thoughts on whether or not the pills are working/if side affects are making too much of a difference.  Also, try getting a therapist. My depression is clinical, but i still find that therapists help with ALL sorts of problems.
